actions.reason: consumer deregistration did not terminate transport within 60s

observations.conclusion: Both repetitions observed zero modeled exception frames on legal same-consumer renewal and consumer deregistration followed by stream-delete fallback. The instrumented repetition observed an HTTP/1.1 zero-length terminal chunk and closed HTTP response for both server-terminated subscriptions, without any client close request. These are server response ends, not decoded modeled exceptions. No universal modeled-error metric rule is established.

deregisteredConsumerDataControl.conclusion: After consumer deregistration and native ResourceNotFound proof, the original still-active subscription delivered a newly accepted PutRecord marker with the exact accepted sequence number. Existing read-session data delivery survives this consumer deletion; this does not imply new subscriptions can be admitted for the deleted consumer or that the session outlives its five-minute lease.

limitations: No ResourceInUseException or ResourceNotFoundException event-stream frame occurred in either repetition. The requested modeled-exception metric boundary remains unobserved; legal renewal documentation expressly allows expiration OR ResourceInUseException. Do not extrapolate terminal EOF observations to modeled-error delivery.

Consumer deregistration did not terminate either active subscription within the 60-second observation window. Each subsequent stream deletion did terminate shortly afterward; temporal association supports a stream-delete fallback observation, not a claim that deregistration itself caused the terminal.

CloudWatch dimensions identify consumer, not subscription session. Renewal-old and renewal-new share the same consumer. Old-only and mixed receive-minute counts are retained, but success samples in the mixed minute cannot be uniquely allocated to either session.

Successful native publication counts exceed the number of normal frames decoded at the client; explicit close can prevent client receipt/decoding of events already successfully published by AWS. Do not substitute decoded frame count for CloudWatch SampleCount or Sum.

Primary-capture transport stream wrapper was installed after boto3 initial-response parsing had already entered the underlying generator and did not activate. Its generator exhaustion alone is not physical EOF proof. The independent repeat dynamically tapped urllib3 chunk-length parsing and recorded actual terminal zero chunks plus HTTP response closure.
HTTP response end is not a claim that the TCP connection died. The transport-confirmed capture negotiated HTTP/1.1 chunked responses via botocore, despite API reference prose describing HTTP/2.

Success one/zero sample counts are derived from native SampleCount and Sum with native extrema 0 and 1; companion zero-valued samples are evidenced by Minimum=Maximum=Sum=0. No decoded exception can be assigned a metric sample in these captures.

All fixed-window requests used one-minute periods, both StreamName and ConsumerName dimensions, all five basic statistics, and no Unit filter. Checkpoint +900s is measured from completion of all terminal captures in that repetition, not from each individual session end.
The concurrent explicit close of renewal-new caused a local AttributeError in urllib3 reading its now-closed response. It is captured as a client-close reader error, never a native modeled exception.

The third data control exercises one immediate post-deregistration accepted record before five-minute expiry. It establishes more than lingering empty heartbeats, but not indefinite lease survival. No CloudWatch sweep was requested for that control.

officialReferenceNotes.observedText: Calling SubscribeToShard >=5 seconds after a successful call lets the new call take over; the previous connection expires or fails with ResourceInUseException.
SubscribeToShardEventStream is a tagged union containing ResourceInUseException and ResourceNotFoundException, among other variants.
DeregisterStreamConsumer describes deletion and HTTP 200 empty response, but does not promise a terminal event or active-subscription termination latency.

SubscribeToShardEvent.Success is described as emitted whenever an event is published successfully; per-consumer dimensions are StreamName, ConsumerName. Docs do not specify zero-sample terminal behavior.
StartTime inclusive and rounded to minute for recent data; EndTime exclusive; all five statistics requested; results sorted in derived views while raw response ordering retained.

reproduction.resourceMode: each repetition uses one empty provisioned shard, no writes, distinct renewal/deregister consumers
reproduction.sequence: Wait active; align minute+5; subscribe original LATEST; wait first frame then 65 seconds; same-consumer same-shard legal renewal LATEST; wait old end <=35 seconds; explicitly close new; distinct consumer subscribe LATEST; wait first event+12seconds; deregister; wait <=60seconds; if still active delete owned stream; observe terminal; clean all owned resources; fixed-window metrics at +0,+60,+180,+300,+600,+900 seconds after terminal-capture completion.
reproduction.retryMode: standard total_max_attempts=1, before-send hook records every actual send; explicit admission retries only ResourceInUseException max10 at2s intervals
reproduction.eventCapture: boto3 EventStream._event_generator messages captured with exact headers/UTF-8 payload, then SDK _parse_event called; continue underlying message generator even after modeled exception so terminal transport is separately observable. Repeat attaches HTTPResponse._update_chunk_length observer after admission, checks chunkLeft=0 and closed native HTTPResponse.
